supporting_observations.claim: Repeated svc-billing failures occurred on FILE-PIN-01 at roughly one-minute intervals from 13:36 through 13:51 UTC. The 4625 events report bad-password substatus 0xc000006a, and the corresponding 4776 events identify FILE-PIN-01 as the workstation.

The failures are consistent with the supplied inventory and change calendar: svc-billing is a BillingSync job on FILE-PIN-01 that re-authenticates every minute, and its password was scheduled for rotation at 13:30 with a manual job update required. The observed regular failures begin after that scheduled rotation.

Some corresponding DC events are Kerberos pre-authentication failures with status 0x18, also consistent with an incorrect password; the records do not show a successful authentication for svc-billing.

known_telemetry_limitations: These records show authentication failures, but do not establish whether or when the password rotation occurred or whether the BillingSync job was subsequently updated.
The 4625 records show LSASS handling the authentication and the source address, but do not identify the application or task that initiated each attempt.
The supplied records do not establish whether any svc-billing authentication succeeded elsewhere in the environment or outside this time window.
claims_not_established: That the failed attempts were initiated by the BillingSync job, rather than another process on FILE-PIN-01.
That the scheduled password rotation was completed at 13:30 UTC.
That the svc-billing credentials were compromised or that an attacker caused these failures.
additional_evidence_needed: Operationally confirm the rotation and manual BillingSync credential update, and verify that the job resumes successful authentication.
unrelated_findings: At 13:20 UTC, WS-ESTONE-01 recorded an explicit-credentials event using svc-billing for target server PROXY-PIN-01, under SYSTEM with taskhostw.exe. This is separate from the later FILE-PIN-01 failure pattern and does not establish that proxy authentication succeeded; review separately. (T092-00001)
